intended_object: The natural transformation from the cycles functor S ↦ Z(S) = ker(S.g) to the second-object projection S ↦ S.X₂, whose component at S is the canonical inclusion of the cycles into X₂. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: This declaration is in Mathlib itself. Its component at each S is `S.iCycles`, the canonical monomorphism from the cycles (a kernel of S.g) into S.X₂. Naturality holds by the lemma `cyclesMap_i`, which the automatic `aesop_cat` naturality proof uses. The assumptions `[HasKernels C] [HasCokernels C]` are needed because `cyclesFunctor` is defined under them: every short complex must have left homology for the cycles functor to exist on all of `ShortComplex C`. So the generality matches what the construction needs, and the definition is the standard inclusion of cycles, made natural in S.
